text: Aesthesia [Gr. aisqhsiV , perception by the senses]: Ger. Empfindlichkeit ; Fr. sensibilité ; Ital. sensibilità , estesia . A synonym of sensibility. As ANAESTHESIA (q.v.) denotes the absence of the capacity to have sensation, so Aesthesia denotes its normal presence. ( J.J. ) The term is also used to denote the general power and process of feeling, in opposition to kinesia, the power of movement. See Arndt, Lehrb . dPsychol ., and Morselli, Semej . malat . ment ., ii. ( E.M. )
